<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **7** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 497518c3f67d8cc022fc6663d2e08f97117298a4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d2b7cef8305a3076d7e32c6854acb427b5145d02` — the merge of head `fcc038d2fb05e6152f7c05431834e0ea06e3f9b8` into base `497518c3f67d8cc022fc6663d2e08f97117298a4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d2b7cef8305a3076d7e32c6854acb427b5145d02 && git checkout d2b7cef8305a3076d7e32c6854acb427b5145d02
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 497518c3f67d8cc022fc6663d2e08f97117298a4 fcc038d2fb05e6152f7c05431834e0ea06e3f9b8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 497518c3f67d8cc022fc6663d2e08f97117298a4 && git merge --no-ff fcc038d2fb05e6152f7c05431834e0ea06e3f9b8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 497518c3f67d8cc022fc6663d2e08f97117298a4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 497518c3f67d8cc022fc6663d2e08f97117298a4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Checklist**
- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #23847`; the other numbers (#17231, #23848) carry no closing verb. `Clause-②: no` on its own line in the body and the changeset.
- **`Clause-②: no` is truthful.** The published contract already declares what this enforces: `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`, `storage.notNull`, "Emit a physical NOT NULL on the column (ADR-0113)." The remote face not emitting it was the defect; the declared accept set does not move. No contract face is hit (no narrowing declaration, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path), so CI plus this in-seat read.
- **Scope.** 4 paths inside the amended claim surface: `remote-transport.ts` (one `columnDeclarationSQL` renderer feeding `buildCreateTableSQL` and both `ADD COLUMN` sites; `executeAddColumn` naming the refused statement on `syncSchema`'s path), the `NOT NULL` sentences of `turso-driver.ts`'s `REMOTE_DRIFT_REPORT_CAVEAT` and its docblock only (the #23848-owned remedy clause and its twin unchanged in the diff; relay 6213357665 kept), the new test, the changeset.
- **Predicate parity.** The remote `declaresColumnNotNull` is the same expression as `driver-sql`'s module-private one (`sql-driver.ts` ~:2034 on `origin/main`): truthiness of `storage.notNull`, never `required`. The test pins the two faces' `notnull` flags equal for one declaration set.
- **Evidence.** Positive control on unchanged code against a real `sqld` 0.24.32 (checksum-verified) and on the libSQL `file:` instrument: both report `tighten_not_null` for the declared fields. After: `[]` on CREATE and ADD COLUMN, the insert refused with `NOT NULL constraint failed`, and the populated-table ADD COLUMN refused on both faces alike. Ablation: the ` NOT NULL` suffix removed turns all 10 cases red. Driver conformance ledger 55 covered, 0 DEBT, before and after (the lane's standing commitment).
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence:** "What was wrong" (remote sync created declared columns nullable; inserts stored; drift read as destructive) matches the control; "What changes" (CREATE and ADD COLUMN add `NOT NULL` wherever the local face does; never for `required`) matches the diff; "What does not change" (existing columns untouched, no data at rest migrated, the caveat reworded, the boot gate still does not act; a populated-table ADD COLUMN refused on both faces; the literal-`defaultValue` asymmetry) matches the test's cases. `patch`: a fix bringing the remote face to the declared contract.
- **Gates on the head.** `ci-failure.mjs --pr 23893`: GREEN, 40 of 40. Six skips are on `check-expected-skips.mjs`'s roster; `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` read `skipped` only on the 11:47 run that this seat's body edit fired, and both read `success` on the 11:42 run of the same head.
- **Landing checks.** `check-governed-merges --pr 23893`: NOT governed, 353 changed lines. `mergeable_state` `clean`; `git merge-tree` against current `origin/main` (`497518c3f`) is clean.

**The dev's open question, answered A by this seat (not escalated):** keep the shipped behaviour. The remote face does not emit declared column DEFAULTs, so a `storage.notNull` field with a literal `defaultValue` added to a populated remote table is refused loudly and names the statement. No in-repo producer declares `storage.notNull` (the dev's grep over `platform-objects`, plugins and examples), and the external case is unmeasured. B (one shared default renderer, exported from `driver-sql`) is the shape to take if a real pull is measured; C (a remote-only default rule) is not taken.
